reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that traditional hockey analytics rely on aggregate game-level stats, which obscure individual contributions. By tracking zone entries and possession events, we derive possession-weighted metrics that isolate skill components. The first primitive, possession-weighted shot differential, corrects for sample size variation by normalizing shots per possession. The second, zone entry method classification, provides granular input for modeling zone-specific behavior. The third, neutral zone performance score, quantifies the dominant influence of neutral zone play on overall shot differential. These primitives form a dual framework: one that separates offensive and defensive contributions (via possession), and another that identifies strategic dominance (via zone entry types). Failure modes include misclassification of possession events or underrepresentation of rare entry types, which can skew the derived scores.
